F001.wording: Gale Crater is a giant bowl on Mars about 154 km (96 miles) wide!

F004.wording: Mars has two tiny moons named Phobos and Deimos.

F007.wording: In Gale Crater, Curiosity measured nighttime ground temperatures dropping to -72°C (-98°F).

F008.wording: In 2018, a giant dust storm covered the entire planet of Mars!

F010.wording: Martian dirt has a little bit of water trapped inside it—about two pints of water in every cubic foot of dirt!

F011.wording: Because Mars is so far away, a message takes anywhere from 3 to 22 minutes to reach Earth.

F014.wording: NOAA and NASA scientists watch the Sun every single day to keep astronauts safe from space weather.

F015.wording: Solar flares are rated by letters like C (small), M (medium), and X (giant!).

F017.wording: Curiosity has a special tool that has been measuring invisible space radiation since it landed.

F019.wording: Mars rocks are sharp! Curiosity's wheels got little holes in them, so NASA had to drive it carefully.

F020.wording: The International Space Station uses tools like a robotic sniffer to help find tiny leaks!

F021.wording: Mars has very thin air, so small space rocks can easily reach the ground and make fresh craters!

F022.wording: NASA is practicing on the Moon right now so humans can safely explore Mars in the future.
